title: Dashboards: operations, evals, delivery and spend
bridge: A Grafana dashboard JSON is like a Storybook story you know. It is a file in git that describes what to show, and a tool renders it. Except nothing in it runs on your laptop. Every panel is a query string that Grafana sends to VictoriaMetrics or VictoriaLogs when someone opens the page.
intro: Lesson g1-2 wrote the series. This lesson builds the four screens that read them. Operations for running agents, spend with a burn-rate alert, the eval scoreboard, and delivery impact at team level. Every dashboard shows agents and teams, never a person.

picture.caption: A JSON file in git becomes a Grafana screen; a rule file becomes a Slack message that never stops anything.

steps.text: a PR adds the file; the sidecar picks up every JSON in the folder
loads it into the AI-Agents folder
each panel runs its expr against the gateway and delivery series
the error and rejection panels query Claude Code events
every hour evaluates the two spend rules
after 6 hours ahead of budget, posts a warning; nothing stops

sections.h: A JSON file becomes a Grafana folder
p: Open the infrastructure repo at modules/grafana/dashboards/. Every folder there holds dashboard JSON files, and a sidecar, a small container next to Grafana, loads every file it finds. The folder name becomes the Grafana folder, so AI-Agents/ai-agents-operations.json shows up under AI-Agents at grafana.example.com. Adding a dashboard is a PR with one new file.

Each file has the same bones. title and uid name it; the uid is the stable id in URLs such as /d/ai-spend. tags group it and time sets the default range. templating lists variables such as $agent, filled by label_values(series, label).

panels is the list of charts. Each has a type, a gridPos (x, y, width and height on a 24-column grid) and targets. A target's expr is a query. For metrics it is PromQL, the Prometheus query language, which VictoriaMetrics runs.

rate(x[6h]) is a counter's per-second growth over 6 hours, and increase(x[1d]) is how much it grew in a day. sum by (agent) adds series up per agent label. For logs the expr is LogsQL, the query language of VictoriaLogs: a filter, then a pipe, then stats by (...) count(). Two panels on the operations dashboard use it; everything else is PromQL.

callout.text: Before you write an expr, open vmui (VictoriaMetrics' own query page) and VictoriaLogs and check the exact series and field names. Prometheus naming adds unit and _total suffixes, so the gateway's cost series is ai_agents_llm_cost_usd_total.

sections.h: Operations part 1: cost and tokens per agent
p: This is the screen we open when something feels off, and in the weekly run review. It shows agents, never people. Cost and tokens come from the gateway series (lesson g0-5); people's Claude Code series are not on it. Lines 1 to 14 of the sketch follow; part 2 has the last three panels.
sections.because: We chart cost and tokens per agent, because a run that burns tokens shows here hours before anyone reads a bill.

code.text:
{
  "title": "AI agents: operations",
  "uid": "ai-agents-ops",
  "tags": ["ai-agents"],
  "time": { "from": "now-7d", "to": "now" },
  "templating": { "list": [ {
    "name": "agent", "type": "query", "multi": true, "includeAll": true,
    "datasource": { "type": "victoriametrics-metrics-datasource" },
    "query": "label_values(ai_agents_llm_cost_usd_total, agent)" } ] },
  "panels": [
    { "title": "Cost per agent, USD per day", "type": "timeseries", "gridPos": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 12, "h": 8 },
      "targets": [ { "expr": "sum by (agent) (increase(ai_agents_llm_cost_usd_total{agent=~\"$agent\"}[1d]))" } ] },
    { "title": "Tokens by type", "type": "timeseries", "gridPos": { "x": 12, "y": 0, "w": 12, "h": 8 },
      "targets": [ { "expr": "sum by (type) (increase(ai_agents_llm_tokens_total{agent=~\"$agent\"}[1h]))" } ] },

notes.text: The title people see in the Grafana list.
uid ai-agents-ops is the stable id; links and alerts point at /d/ai-agents-ops.
Default range: the last 7 days.
A variable named agent, filled by a query, with multi-select and an All option.
The datasource type is the VictoriaMetrics plugin, not the generic Prometheus one.
label_values lists every agent label on the cost series, so a new agent appears with no edit.
First panel: a timeseries chart at the top left, 12 of 24 columns wide and 8 rows high.
increase over 1 day of the cost counter, summed per agent; agent=~"$agent" applies the variable (=~ is a regex match).
Second panel, top right.
Tokens by type over 1 hour; the type label is input, output, cache_read or cache_write.

sections.h: Operations part 2: cache share, errors, rejections
p: The prompt cache lets Claude reuse the start of a prompt it has seen before, at a lower price. The cache-read share is the part of all input tokens that came from the cache. Under 70% it turns red: a model switch, a changing tool list or a timestamp in the prompt breaks the cache. Lines 15 to 26 of the sketch follow; they continue the panels array.
Errors and rejected tool calls are events, not metrics. Claude Code sends them to VictoriaLogs through the collector (lesson g1-1), so these two panels switch datasource to the logs plugin.
sections.because: We show cache share, errors and rejected tools together, because each is an early sign of a run going wrong.

code.text:
{ "title": "Cache-read share (healthy at 80% or more)", "type": "stat", "gridPos": { "x": 0, "y": 8, "w": 6, "h": 6 },
      "fieldConfig": { "defaults": { "unit": "percentunit", "thresholds": { "mode": "absolute", "steps": [
        { "color": "red", "value": null }, { "color": "yellow", "value": 0.7 }, { "color": "green", "value": 0.8 } ] } } },
      "targets": [ { "expr": "sum(rate(ai_agents_llm_tokens_total{type=\"cache_read\",agent=~\"$agent\"}[6h])) / sum(rate(ai_agents_llm_tokens_total{type=~\"input|cache_read|cache_write\",agent=~\"$agent\"}[6h]))" } ] },
    { "title": "API errors", "type": "timeseries", "gridPos": { "x": 6, "y": 8, "w": 9, "h": 6 },
      "datasource": { "type": "victoriametrics-logs-datasource" },
      "targets": [ { "expr": "event.name:api_error agent:~\"$agent\" | stats by (agent, status_code) count()" } ] },
    { "title": "Rejected tool calls", "type": "timeseries", "gridPos": { "x": 15, "y": 8, "w": 9, "h": 6 },
      "datasource": { "type": "victoriametrics-logs-datasource" },
      "targets": [ { "expr": "event.name:tool_decision decision:reject agent:~\"$agent\" | stats by (agent, tool_name) count()" } ] }
  ]
}

notes.text: A stat panel: one big number with a colour, 6 columns wide.
percentunit shows 0.8 as 80%; thresholds pick the colour in absolute mode.
Red from 0, yellow from 0.7, green from 0.8: the title says healthy at 80% or more.
Cache-read tokens over 6 hours divided by all input-side tokens (input, cache_read, cache_write) over the same 6 hours.
API errors as a timeseries of counts.
This panel's datasource is the VictoriaLogs plugin, so its expr is LogsQL, not PromQL.
Filter events named api_error for the chosen agents, then count them per agent and status_code.
Rejected tool calls: a wall that fires often shows here.
tool_decision events whose decision is reject, counted per agent and tool_name.
The panels array closes; G1-15 adds its failure-label panel above this line with its own gridPos.

p: We control tokens with visibility first. The spend dashboard, AI-Agents/ai-spend.json, has four views. People's spend by team comes from claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total, and agent spend by agent from the gateway. Cost per ticket uses the gateway series by jira, and cost per merged agent PR uses the merged PR keys from G1-07.

No panel has a person dimension. Each person sees their own spend in /usage and the status line only. The nightly job writes two more series per scope: ai_spend_mtd_usd, the month-to-date spend, and ai_spend_budget_usd, the month's budget from settings/spend-limits.yaml (lesson g0-6). Scopes are people, and each agent.
Burn rate means how fast the budget is being used. The plan is a straight line from 0 on day 1 to the budget on the last day. Spend 25% above that line fires the alert.

The rule file lives in the victoria-metrics unit of the infrastructure repo, under alerting/templates/alert_rules/. Open the files already there and copy their shape: the sketch is a list of groups that the unit wraps for vmalert. Lines 2 to 21 of the sketch follow; the file-path comment is dropped and part 2 holds the second rule.
sections.because: We alert at 25% ahead of the budget line, because a bad month must be caught while there is time to act.

code.text:
---

- name: ai-spend
  interval: 1h
  rules:
    - alert: AISpendAheadOfBudget
      # Month-to-date spend more than 25% ahead of a straight line to the monthly budget.
      expr: |-
        sum by (scope) (ai_spend_mtd_usd)
          > 1.25 * sum by (scope) (ai_spend_budget_usd) * day_of_month() / days_in_month()
      for: 6h
      labels:
        severity: warning
        cloud.account.name: inf
        service.name: ai-agents
        service.component: spend
      annotations:
        summary: "[AI spend «{{ $labels.scope }}»] month-to-date is more than 25% ahead of budget"
        description: "An alert, never a stop. The AI spend dashboard shows which teams or agents drive it."
        external_link: "https://grafana.example.com/d/ai-spend"

notes.text: A rule group named ai-spend; vmalert evaluates a group's rules together.
Every hour is enough: the input series change once a night.
The alert's name, as it appears in Slack and in Grafana.
|- starts a multi-line string, so the expression can be read on two lines.
Month-to-date spend, summed per scope (people, or one agent).
The budget line: budget times the day of the month, divided by the days in the month, times 1.25.
The condition must hold for 6 hours before the alert fires, so one odd sample pages nobody.
severity warning: a message, not a wake-up.
These three labels follow the existing rules in the folder; the alertmanager route matches on them to reach #ai-agents-alerts.
The Slack line, with the scope filled in from the series labels.
The annotation says it in words: an alert, never a stop.
A link straight to the spend dashboard, uid ai-spend.

callout.text: day_of_month() and days_in_month() return series with no labels. Check in vmui that the whole expression returns one series per scope. If it returns nothing, the label matching needs on() group_left; check the MetricsQL docs for binary operations.

sections.h: Spend part 2: the cache rule and the route
p: The second rule watches the same cache-read share as the operations panel, per agent. Under 70% for 2 hours it warns, because a cold cache costs real money every turn. Lines 22 to 33 of the sketch follow.

Route both rules to #ai-agents-alerts with a mention of Sean and Nir, in the alertmanager config of the same unit. Copy an existing route and match on service.name: ai-agents. Add what drives the spend to the message: the top 3 teams or agents by week-over-week growth, read from the dashboard.
sections.because: We alert on a cold prompt cache too, because it is the most common silent cause of a spend jump.

code.text:
- alert: AICacheReadShareLow
      expr: |-
        sum by (agent) (rate(ai_agents_llm_tokens_total{type="cache_read"}[6h]))
          / sum by (agent) (rate(ai_agents_llm_tokens_total{type=~"input|cache_read|cache_write"}[6h])) < 0.70
      for: 2h
      labels:
        severity: warning
        cloud.account.name: inf
        service.name: ai-agents
        service.component: spend
      annotations:
        summary: "[AI agent «{{ $labels.agent }}»] reads under 70% of its input from the prompt cache"

notes.text: The second rule in the same group.
Cache-read tokens per agent, as a rate over 6 hours.
Divided by all input-side tokens; below 0.70 the rule is true. Same maths as the operations stat panel.
2 hours of a cold cache before it warns; one short run with a new tool list is not worth a message.
The same service.name label, so the same route carries it.
The Slack line names the agent; the fix is in the harness, not in Grafana.

sections.h: Evals part 1: suite and split variables
p: Every rule, prompt and model change has to hold up in the evals, the fixed test sets from lesson p12-3. The scoreboard, AI-Agents/ai-evals.json, has one row per suite. It shows pass rate with its spread, cost per case and median turns, per version, model and effort. The series come from G1-08's eval store; the nightly job writes them from JSON files in S3.

Spread is how much the pass rate moves between the 3 runs of each case. A change only counts when it moves past the low edge, pass rate minus spread. Lines 1 to 10 of the sketch follow: the header and the two variables.
sections.because: We put suite and split in variables, because one panel definition then repeats per suite and serves all four splits.

code.text:
{
  "title": "AI agents: eval scoreboard",
  "uid": "ai-evals",
  "tags": ["ai-agents", "evals"],
  "templating": { "list": [
    { "name": "suite", "type": "query", "multi": true, "includeAll": true,
      "datasource": { "type": "victoriametrics-metrics-datasource" },
      "query": "label_values(ai_agents_eval_pass_rate, suite)" },
    { "name": "split", "type": "custom", "query": "dev,holdout,smoke,full",
      "current": { "text": "dev", "value": "dev" } } ] },

notes.text: uid ai-evals: the link the routing-table PR (G1-17) points at.
Two tags, so the dashboard is found under ai-agents and under evals.
suite is a query variable with multi-select; the panels repeat once per selected suite.
The suites are read from the suite label of ai_agents_eval_pass_rate, so a new suite appears by itself.
split is a custom variable with four fixed values: dev, holdout, smoke, full (G1-08's schema).
dev is selected by default; holdout is the split you look at before a release.

sections.h: Evals part 2: pass rate, low edge, cost, turns
p: Two panels, each repeated per suite. The first draws the pass rate per version, model and effort, with a second line for the low edge. The second is a table with cost per case and median turns next to each pass rate. A right answer reached the long way still shows.

The ticket also asks for a data link from each point to its S3 JSON key. One click then opens the run's cause labels. Grafana adds it under fieldConfig.defaults.links; check the Grafana docs for data links and the URL field they expect. Lines 11 to 28 of the sketch follow.
sections.because: We draw the low edge next to the pass rate, because a change inside the spread is noise, not progress.

code.text:
"panels": [
    { "title": "$suite: pass rate (band = spread of 3 runs)", "type": "timeseries", "repeat": "suite",
      "gridPos": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 12, "h": 8 },
      "fieldConfig": { "defaults": { "unit": "percentunit", "min": 0, "max": 1 } },
      "targets": [
        { "refId": "A", "legendFormat": "{{version}} {{model}} {{effort}}",
          "expr": "max by (version, model, effort) (ai_agents_eval_pass_rate{suite=\"$suite\", split=\"$split\"})" },
        { "refId": "B", "legendFormat": "{{version}} low edge",
          "expr": "max by (version, model, effort) (ai_agents_eval_pass_rate{suite=\"$suite\", split=\"$split\"} - ai_agents_eval_pass_rate_spread{suite=\"$suite\", split=\"$split\"})" } ] },
    { "title": "$suite: cost per case and median turns", "type": "table", "repeat": "suite",
      "gridPos": { "x": 12, "y": 0, "w": 12, "h": 8 },
      "targets": [
        { "refId": "C", "format": "table", "instant": true,
          "expr": "max by (version, model, effort) (ai_agents_eval_cost_per_case_usd{suite=\"$suite\", split=\"$split\"})" },
        { "refId": "D", "format": "table", "instant": true,
          "expr": "max by (version, model, effort) (ai_agents_eval_median_turns{suite=\"$suite\", split=\"$split\"})" } ] }
  ]
}

notes.text: $suite in the title and repeat: suite make Grafana draw one copy per selected suite.
Pass rate is a fraction from 0 to 1; percentunit shows it as a percentage with a fixed axis.
legendFormat names each line by its version, model and effort labels.
max by keeps one point per version, model and effort for the chosen suite and split.
The low edge: pass rate minus the spread series, same labels.
A table, repeated per suite, to the right of the chart.
format table with instant true asks for the latest value only, one row per combination.
Cost per case in USD, so a cheaper setting that holds its pass rate shows up.
Median turns: a right answer reached in 40 turns is a worse setting than one reached in 12.

sections.h: Delivery impact part 1: review wait and failure
p: This dashboard answers 'is it helping?' at team level only. It reads the delivery_* series from lesson g1-2 and draws the September baseline as a reference line on each panel. Throughput alone rewards the wrong thing, so merged PRs never appear without change failure beside them. Lines 1 to 14 of the sketch follow.
Weekly numbers for about 25 engineers are noisy. Show counts next to medians, add a text note saying so, and default the range to 12 weeks. Walk Nir through it before it is shared.
sections.because: We draw merged PRs and change failure on one panel, because more merges with more failures is not an improvement.

code.text:
{
  "title": "Delivery impact (team level)",
  "uid": "delivery-impact",
  "tags": ["ai-agents", "delivery"],
  "time": { "from": "now-12w", "to": "now" },
  "templating": { "list": [ {
    "name": "team", "type": "query", "multi": true, "includeAll": true,
    "datasource": { "type": "victoriametrics-metrics-datasource" },
    "query": "label_values(delivery_review_wait_hours, team)" } ] },
  "panels": [
    { "title": "Review wait, hours (p50 and p85)", "type": "timeseries", "gridPos": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 12, "h": 8 },
      "targets": [
        { "refId": "A", "legendFormat": "{{team}} {{q}}", "expr": "max by (team, q) (delivery_review_wait_hours{team=~\"$team\"})" },
        { "refId": "B", "legendFormat": "baseline {{q}}", "expr": "max by (q) (delivery_baseline_review_wait_hours)" } ] },

notes.text: Default range 12 weeks: the same length as the baseline.
A team variable with multi-select and All; there is no person variable anywhere.
Teams are read from the team label of delivery_review_wait_hours.
Review wait in hours; p50 and p85 come from the q label and draw on one chart.
max by (team, q) over the weekly series, filtered by the team variable; the legend reads 'frontend p85' and so on.
The baseline series from the backfill, one reference line per q.

callout.text: A series with one point draws one dot, not a line. Check the baseline spans the whole 12-week range. If it does not, the backfill must write the baseline value at every week's timestamp.

sections.h: Delivery impact part 2: PRs, lead time, red main
p: Lines 15 to 28 follow. The merged-PRs panel has two targets on two axes: a count on the left and a percentage on the right. Lead time compares cohorts, agent against human PRs, by the cohort label the nightly job writes. Red-main hours per week is a bar chart from the ci.ts numbers.

The sketch shows four panels. The real file adds the rows the ticket lists: a baseline line on each panel and counts next to medians. Then the agent rows (merge rate, human rework, CI auto-fix success), which start as 'no data'.
sections.because: We put the percentage on a right axis, because the reader must see count and failure move together or apart.

code.text:
{ "title": "Merged PRs next to change failure", "type": "timeseries", "gridPos": { "x": 12, "y": 0, "w": 12, "h": 8 },
      "targets": [
        { "refId": "A", "legendFormat": "merged PRs", "expr": "sum(delivery_merged_prs{team=~\"$team\"})" },
        { "refId": "B", "legendFormat": "change failure %",
          "expr": "100 * sum(delivery_failed_changes{team=~\"$team\"}) / sum(delivery_merged_prs{team=~\"$team\"})" } ],
      "fieldConfig": { "defaults": {}, "overrides": [ { "matcher": { "id": "byName", "options": "change failure %" },
        "properties": [ { "id": "custom.axisPlacement", "value": "right" }, { "id": "unit", "value": "percent" } ] } ] } },
    { "title": "Lead time, hours: agent vs. human PRs", "type": "timeseries", "gridPos": { "x": 0, "y": 8, "w": 12, "h": 8 },
      "targets": [ { "refId": "A", "legendFormat": "{{cohort}}",
        "expr": "max by (cohort) (delivery_lead_time_hours{q=\"p50\", team=~\"$team\"})" } ] },
    { "title": "Hours main stayed red, per week", "type": "barchart", "gridPos": { "x": 12, "y": 8, "w": 12, "h": 8 },
      "targets": [ { "refId": "A", "expr": "sum(delivery_red_main_hours)" } ] }
  ]
}

notes.text: Merged PRs next to change failure: one panel, on purpose.
Merged PRs per week, summed over the selected teams.
Change failure as a percentage: failed changes divided by merged PRs, times 100.
An override picks the series by its legend name, change failure %.
Two properties for that series: draw it on the right axis and show it as a percent.
Lead time in hours, p50 only, one line per cohort.
cohort is a label the nightly job sets to agent or human by PR author.
A barchart, one bar per week.
Hours main stayed red per week, summed; no team label, because main is shared.

lab.title: Grafana and VictoriaMetrics on your laptop

worked.do: mkdir grafana-lab && cd grafana-lab && mkdir -p provisioning/datasources provisioning/dashboards dashboards rules

Create compose.yaml:
services:
  victoriametrics:
    image: victoriametrics/victoria-metrics:latest
    ports: ["8428:8428"]

      - ./provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning

quiz.q: The cache-read share stat shows 55%. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The agent read many files, so input tokens went up.
options.why: File reads add input tokens, but the shared prefix is still served from the cache; the share stays high.

options.text: Something changes the start of the prompt each turn: a model switch, a changing tool list or a timestamp.
options.why: The cache matches the start of the prompt byte for byte; any change there breaks it.
Both sides of the ratio come from the same series over the same 6 hours; lost samples would not move the share.

quiz.q: AISpendAheadOfBudget fires on the 10th of the month. What happens next?

options.text: Sean and Nir get a message in #ai-agents-alerts with what drives the spend, and they decide.
options.why: The rule's annotation says it: an alert, never a stop; the dashboard shows which teams or agents drive it.

options.text: The gateway stops agent runs for that scope until the month ends.
options.why: No limit cuts a run; spend is controlled with visibility first.

options.text: Each person over budget gets a direct message.
options.why: No alert and no panel has a person dimension; people see their own spend in /usage only.

quiz.q: Where does a new dashboard go?

options.text: Build it in the Grafana UI and click save.
options.why: The sidecar overwrites provisioned dashboards from git; UI edits are lost on the next sync.

options.text: A new Terraform helm_release unit per dashboard.
options.why: The Grafana module already runs the sidecar; one file is enough.

options.text: A new JSON file under modules/grafana/dashboards/AI-Agents/ in the infrastructure repo, by PR.
options.why: The sidecar loads every JSON file there, and the folder name becomes the Grafana folder.

videos.title: Server Monitoring // Prometheus and Grafana Tutorial
videos.why: Very popular hands-on setup of Prometheus scraping and a Grafana dashboard.

words.plain: A small container next to Grafana that loads every dashboard JSON file from a folder; the folder name becomes the Grafana folder.
The Prometheus query language that VictoriaMetrics runs: rate, increase and sum by over series.
The query language of VictoriaLogs: a filter, then a pipe to stats by (...) count().
A dropdown such as $agent or $team, filled by label_values, that every panel's query can use.
The part of input tokens served from the prompt cache; healthy at 80% or more, red under 70%.
How fast the month's budget is being used, compared with a straight line to the budget.
How much a pass rate moves between the 3 runs of each eval case; a change inside it is noise.

tickets.why: This lesson read the operations JSON panel by panel: gateway series for cost and tokens, VictoriaLogs for errors and rejections.
walk: Check the exact series and field names in vmui and VictoriaLogs first; Prometheus naming adds unit and _total suffixes.
Add modules/grafana/dashboards/AI-Agents/ai-agents-operations.json in the infrastructure repo from the two blocks above; the sidecar loads it into the AI-Agents folder.
Point cost and tokens at the gateway series only; people's Claude Code series stay off this dashboard.
Point the API errors and rejected tool calls panels at VictoriaLogs (api_error, and tool_decision with decision reject), per agent.
Keep the cache-read thresholds (red under 70%, green from 80%), open the PR and ask DevOps, the co-owner, to review.

tickets.why: This lesson walked through the two alert rules and the spend views that never show a person.
walk: Add AI-Agents/ai-spend.json with five views: people's spend by team (claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total), agent spend by agent, cost per ticket (gateway series by jira). Then cost per merged agent PR (merged PR keys from G1-07) and cache-read share.
In the nightly job (ai-agents/metrics), write ai_spend_mtd_usd and ai_spend_budget_usd per scope (people, and each agent) from settings/spend-limits.yaml.

Add the two rules from the blocks above as infrastructure/multi_tenant/accounts/infrastructure/victoria-metrics/alerting/templates/alert_rules/ai-spend.yml, matching the shape of the files already there.
Route them to #ai-agents-alerts, mentioning Sean and Nir, in the alertmanager config of the same unit. Include the top 3 teams or agents by week-over-week growth.
Check in vmui that the budget expression returns one series per scope before the PR; a person applies the unit.

tickets.why: This lesson explained the suite and split variables and the low-edge line the scoreboard draws.
walk: Wait for G1-08's nightly job to write ai_agents_eval_pass_rate, _pass_rate_spread, _cost_per_case_usd and _median_turns with suite, version, split, model and effort labels.
Add AI-Agents/ai-evals.json from the two blocks above; add a model variable the same way as suite.
Add a data link from each point to its S3 JSON key (fieldConfig.defaults.links; check the Grafana docs). The cause labels are then one click away.
Open it after BYTE-GOLD (G2) and TICKET-BENCH (G4) write their first results. Check one suite's pass rate against its JSON by hand.

tickets.why: This lesson built the team-level delivery view with the baseline line and the two-axis PR panel.
walk: Add AI-Agents/delivery-impact.json from the two blocks above, with the team variable and no person variable anywhere.
Add the remaining rows: lead time agent vs human and red-main hours. Then merge rate, human rework and CI auto-fix success, which show 'no data' until agents run.
Draw the delivery_baseline_* series as a reference line on each panel and check it spans the whole 12-week range.
Show counts next to medians and add a text panel saying weekly numbers are noisy at our size; default range now-12w.
Walk Nir through it before it is shared.

remember: Dashboards are JSON files in git showing agents and teams, never people; the spend alert warns, never stops.
